project.name: layer3-trading-engine
project.description: Autonomous trading engine — Layer 3 (execution) — with a zero-runtime-dependency core in src/ (risk guardrails, supervisor, snapshot, features, regime, gold, execution, orchestration) and an optional Textual/Rich terminal operations console in ops/. The repository also carries a large markdown knowledge corpus: dev_graph/ (an ontology-governed engineering digital twin) plus wiki/ and raw/ domain knowledge, and a React/Vite jarvis/ HUD. Note: this project has over 100 source files; consider scoping analysis to a subdirectory for faster results.

nodes.name: __init__.py
nodes.summary: Package barrel for the Paper-Trading Runtime (MOD-007) that re-exports the public API — evaluate, run_once/run_sequence, runtime models, config, and guard predicates — into a single import surface.
nodes.languageNotes: Python package barrel using explicit re-exports and an __all__ allowlist to define the public API.

nodes.name: config.py
nodes.summary: Defines the immutable RuntimePolicyConfig dataclass and its deterministic fingerprint, controlling which L3 admission guards (operational, snapshot, cooldown) are required and the cooldown window.
nodes.languageNotes: Frozen dataclass with __post_init__ validation and a sha256 policy fingerprint for reproducible runtime-policy versioning.

nodes.name: engine.py
nodes.summary: Pure runtime admission core: evaluate() runs the stateful and snapshot-derived L3 guards over a Gold DecisionPacket, produces a RuntimeDecisionRecord, and appends a deterministic entry to the runtime ledger without mutating inputs.
nodes.languageNotes: Side-effect-free evaluation function — all IO is delegated to runtime.py, keeping the core deterministically testable.

nodes.name: models.py
nodes.summary: Core data contracts for the paper-trading runtime: Verdict enum, GuardOutcome, OperationalInput, the append-only RuntimeLedger with LedgerEntry, and the RuntimeDecisionRecord, plus deterministic hashing helpers for record IDs and snapshot-guard digests.
nodes.languageNotes: Frozen dataclasses with strict from_dict/from_mapping contract validation and sha256-based state hashing for ledger integrity and replay safety.

nodes.name: predicates.py
nodes.summary: Boolean guard predicates for runtime admission — duplicate_ok, operational_ok, data_ok, freshness_ok, and cooldown_ok — that decide whether a decision packet may be admitted given prior ledger state and operational input.

nodes.name: runtime.py
nodes.summary: IO boundary for the paper-trading runtime: loads/persists the append-only ledger and operational input from disk and drives run_once/run_sequence over the pure evaluate() core.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses atomic write-then-os.replace for crash-safe ledger persistence.

nodes.name: alpaca_clock_feed.py
nodes.summary: Operational feed adapter that derives a venue-open/closed OperationalInput from the Alpaca trading-calendar API, with an env-driven factory that enforces paper-trading base URLs.
nodes.languageNotes: Protocol-based AlpacaCalendarClient seam allows injecting a fake calendar in tests while the REST client uses urllib directly.

nodes.name: RuntimePolicyConfig
nodes.summary: Immutable runtime-policy configuration toggling required admission guards and the cooldown window, with validation and a deterministic sha256 fingerprint for policy versioning.

nodes.name: load_config
nodes.summary: Loads and validates a RuntimePolicyConfig from a JSON file, raising RuntimePolicyConfigError on missing files or malformed JSON.

nodes.name: evaluate
nodes.summary: Pure admission core that evaluates all L3 guards against a decision packet, operational input, and prior ledger, then emits a RuntimeDecisionRecord and an appended ledger reflecting the verdict.

nodes.name: _required_guards
nodes.summary: Computes the set of guard names that must pass given the runtime policy configuration's required-guard toggles.

nodes.name: OperationalInput
nodes.summary: Versioned operational-state contract (tradeable, venue_open, halt, degraded) with a deterministic fingerprint, a closed() factory, and strict from_mapping validation.

nodes.name: LedgerEntry
nodes.summary: Single append-only runtime ledger record capturing the verdict, triggered guard, and provenance digests for one decision packet, with to_dict/from_dict serialization.

nodes.name: RuntimeLedger
nodes.summary: Self-describing append-only ledger of admission decisions providing admit-history queries (has_admit, last_admit_as_of), sequencing, immutable append, and a sha256 state hash for chaining.

nodes.name: RuntimeDecisionRecord
nodes.summary: Emitted SCHEMA-012 decision record summarizing a runtime admission outcome — verdict, triggered guard, guard outcomes, ledger state hashes, and non-execution notice — with post-init contract validation.

nodes.name: GuardOutcome
nodes.summary: Immutable result of a single admission guard recording its name, pass/fail status, and reason, with dict serialization.

nodes.name: compute_record_id
nodes.summary: Derives a deterministic sha256 record ID from the source packet, runtime-policy fingerprint, operational fingerprint, snapshot-guard digest, and prior ledger state hash for replay-safe identity.

nodes.name: cooldown_ok
nodes.summary: Cooldown guard that admits a packet only if enough hours have elapsed since the last admitted decision, parsing ledger and packet timestamps and respecting the configured cooldown window.

nodes.name: operational_ok
nodes.summary: Operational guard that fails admission when the venue is closed, halted, or degraded for the packet's instrument based on the operational input.

nodes.name: run_once
nodes.summary: Drives a single admission cycle: loads the ledger and operational input from disk, runs evaluate(), and persists the resulting ledger atomically.

nodes.name: run_sequence
nodes.summary: Replays a sequence of packet/operational pairs through evaluate() against an in-memory ledger, returning the accumulated decision records.

nodes.name: load_ledger
nodes.summary: Loads a RuntimeLedger from a JSON file, returning an empty ledger when the file is absent and raising RuntimeContractError on malformed content.

nodes.name: load_operational
nodes.summary: Loads an OperationalInput from disk for the given instrument, defaulting to a closed-venue input when the file is missing.

nodes.name: AlpacaClockFeed
nodes.summary: Operational feed that queries an injected Alpaca calendar client to produce an OperationalInput reflecting whether the trading venue is open for the target instrument on a given date.

nodes.name: _AlpacaRestCalendarClient
nodes.summary: Concrete Alpaca calendar client that fetches trading days from the Alpaca REST calendar endpoint over urllib and returns them as a tuple of date strings.

nodes.name: clock_feed_from_env
nodes.summary: Factory that builds an AlpacaClockFeed from environment-provided Alpaca credentials and base URL, enforcing a paper-trading base URL guard.

nodes.name: decision_engine.py
nodes.summary: Implements the deterministic DecisionEngine (MOD-002) that scores candidate upgrades against an EvaluationScorecard under treasury and institutional-memory constraints and emits a DecisionPacket.
nodes.languageNotes: Deterministic ranking via stable sort key (-score, upgrade_id) ensures identical inputs yield identical packets.

nodes.name: models.py
nodes.summary: Frozen-dataclass value objects for the Decision Engine, realizing the EvaluationScorecard input contract (SCHEMA-005) and DecisionPacket/RankedOption output contract (SCHEMA-004) plus internal treasury and config types.
nodes.languageNotes: Dependency-free frozen dataclasses enforce invariants via __post_init__ guards (e.g., blocked options must carry a reason).

nodes.name: scoring.py
nodes.summary: Pure deterministic scoring functions that rate an upgrade option by the severity of the office's weakness in the targeted dimension, weighted by expected improvement and cost efficiency.
nodes.languageNotes: Dimension-to-weakness function dispatch via a module-level dict registry (WEAKNESS_DIMENSIONS).

nodes.name: DecisionEngine
nodes.summary: Core engine that scores every upgrade in the catalog, applies exclusion and budget filters, deterministically ranks the options, and selects the best allowed upgrade or signals a no-op.

nodes.name: EvaluationScorecard
nodes.summary: Frozen dataclass realizing SCHEMA-005, carrying realized PnL, calibration, drawdown, and disagreement as the performance evidence consumed by the Decision API.

nodes.name: UpgradeOption
nodes.summary: Frozen dataclass describing a candidate upgrade in the catalog with its id, cost, target weakness dimension, and expected improvement.

nodes.name: TreasuryState
nodes.summary: Immutable treasury snapshot exposing available funds (budget minus deployed) and an after_spend method that returns a new state with the amount deployed.

nodes.name: RankedOption
nodes.summary: One scored option within a decision packet, enforcing the invariant that blocked options carry a reason and allowed options do not via __post_init__ validation.

nodes.name: DecisionPacket
nodes.summary: Frozen dataclass realizing SCHEMA-004, the deterministic decision output, validating that any non-null selected upgrade id references an allowed ranked option.

nodes.name: DecisionConfig
nodes.summary: Configuration holding the early-exit thresholds (promotable PnL and calibration) that let the engine skip upgrades when the office is already performing well.

nodes.name: weakness_severity
nodes.summary: Returns the [0, 1] severity of the office's weakness in a given dimension by dispatching to the registered weakness function, or 0 for unknown dimensions.

nodes.name: score_option
nodes.summary: Computes the cost-efficiency-weighted score of an upgrade option as weakness severity times expected improvement divided by cost, rejecting non-positive costs.

nodes.name: __init__.py
nodes.summary: Package barrel for the Snapshot Consumer (MOD-003), the Layer-3 ingestion boundary; re-exports the consume gate functions and the read-only snapshot contract models.
nodes.languageNotes: Python package barrel using __all__ to declare the public surface of the snapshot_consumer module.

nodes.name: consumer.py
nodes.summary: Implements the Layer-3 side of the Snapshot API (INT-001) as a fail-closed gate: loads, validates, and yields a Layer-2 snapshot only when its quality gate passed and it is not forced or dry-run, returning None otherwise.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses PEP 604 union return types (Snapshot | None) and a fail-closed pattern where absence and rejection both surface as None while structural faults raise.

nodes.name: models.py
nodes.summary: Read-only frozen dataclass models mirroring the Layer-2 Snapshot contract (SCHEMA-001), including per-series values, quality guards, summaries, and the top-level Snapshot with deterministic id recomputation.
nodes.languageNotes: Stdlib-only frozen dataclasses with from_dict factory classmethods that fail-closed via a shared _require helper; snapshot id is recomputed deterministically with hashlib.sha256 over sorted series lines.

nodes.name: load_snapshot
nodes.summary: Loads and parses a snapshot JSON file, returning None for legitimate absence but raising on contract violations so upstream truth-layer faults are surfaced loudly.

nodes.name: is_consumable
nodes.summary: Fail-closed predicate deciding whether Layer-3 may act on a snapshot: requires a passing verdict and snapshot_ok guard and rejects forced bypasses and dry-run previews.

nodes.name: consume
nodes.summary: Single Layer-3 entry point that returns a consumable snapshot or None, composing load_snapshot and is_consumable while letting structural faults propagate as errors.

nodes.name: SeriesValue
nodes.summary: Frozen dataclass for a single point-in-time series observation within a snapshot, with a from_grouped_entry factory and a deterministic _id_line used in snapshot id recomputation.

nodes.name: Guards
nodes.summary: Frozen dataclass capturing the snapshot quality-gate guard flags (snapshot_ok, freshness, revision risk, supervisor veto, etc.) with a from_dict factory that the consumer checks before acting.

nodes.name: QualitySummary
nodes.summary: Frozen dataclass summarising tier-1/tier-2 quality counts and revision-risk series for a snapshot, built from the payload via a from_dict factory.

nodes.name: Snapshot
nodes.summary: Top-level frozen dataclass modelling the Layer-2 Snapshot contract; parses the full payload via from_dict and deterministically recomputes and verifies its snapshot_id with a sha256 hash over sorted series lines.

nodes.summary: Runs export_graph_json.py and throws on any nonzero exit code, relying on the exporter's reliable exit status to detect crashes.

tour.title: Project Overview & Bounded Contexts
tour.description: There is no root README, so start here for orientation. The dev_graph README explains that this repository is an autonomous Layer-3 trading engine documented by a typed engineering knowledge graph, while the Context Map names the six bounded contexts that make up the system: Data Pipeline, Trading Engine, Risk Control, Agent Runtime, Evaluation Loop, and Supervisor Office. Together they give you the project's purpose and the vocabulary used in every later step.

tour.title: The Three-Layer Architecture
tour.description: Building on the bounded contexts, the Layer Model document explains the vertical decomposition the whole codebase is organized around: L1 Data Ingestion, L2 Analysis & Strategy (the snapshot layer, the single source of market truth), and L3 Execution (this repository). Understanding that this engine consumes an upstream L2 snapshot and mediates orders to an L4 broker is the key mental model for reading the pipeline that follows.

tour.title: The Chain Orchestrator Entry Point
tour.description: This is the runtime heart of the engine and the top of the dependency graph. runtime.py is the CLI entry point that locates a snapshot, loads ledger and portfolio state, drives the pipeline via run_chain, and persists results; engine.py wires the six deterministic stages together in order. Every core module the rest of the tour visits is reached by following imports outward from these two files.
tour.languageLesson: The orchestrator separates an impure IO shell (runtime.py: reads snapshots, writes ledgers) from a pure wiring core (engine.py). This functional-core/imperative-shell split is what makes the chain replayable and deterministic — the same inputs always produce the same ChainResult.

tour.title: Stage 1 - Snapshot Ingestion
tour.description: The pipeline's first stage is the Layer-3 side of the Snapshot API, the boundary where upstream market truth enters the engine. The consumer is a fail-closed gate: it loads and validates a Layer-2 snapshot and only yields it when the snapshot's quality gate passed and it is not forced or dry-run, otherwise returning None. This fail-closed posture is the first of many guardrails you will see throughout the engine.

tour.title: Stage 2 - Feature Building
tour.description: Once a snapshot is admitted, the feature builder turns it into a deterministic feature vector by applying declarative FeatureSpec transforms (price levels and spreads) while tracking provenance and staleness. This is the engine's transition from raw market data to the structured signals every downstream decision relies on. The declarative-spec approach keeps the transform list auditable and the output reproducible.

tour.title: Stage 3 - Regime Classification
tour.description: The feature vector from Step 5 is fed into the regime classifier, which evaluates a prioritized taxonomy of rules to label the current market regime, recording matched, secondary, and near-miss rules with their margins. The taxonomy module defines those per-regime predicate functions and margin-scoring helpers. This deterministic rule-based classification (rather than a black-box model) is a deliberate design choice captured in the regime ADR.

tour.title: Stage 4 - Gold Decision Packet
tour.description: With features and a regime in hand, the decision builder assembles the GoldDecisionPacket: it computes a trust score, resolves a trade direction, attaches a rationale and guard references, and stamps a content-addressed packet id. The policy module holds the scoring policy that derives that trust score and confidence inputs. This packet is the engine's central decision artifact and the highest-fan-in model in the entire codebase, so it is worth studying closely.
tour.languageLesson: The packet id is content-addressed — derived by hashing the decision's inputs — so identical inputs yield an identical id. This is the same idea behind Git commit hashes and lets the system deduplicate and verify decisions without a database.

tour.title: Stage 5 - Paper-Trading Runtime Admission
tour.description: Before a decision can trade, the paper-trading runtime decides whether to admit it. The pure evaluate() core runs stateful and snapshot-derived L3 guards (cooldowns, duplicates, operational state) over the Gold packet, produces a RuntimeDecisionRecord, and appends a deterministic entry to an append-only ledger without mutating its inputs. The runtime module is the IO boundary that loads and persists that ledger around the pure core.
tour.languageLesson: The append-only ledger is an event-sourcing pattern: state is never overwritten, only appended. Replaying the ledger from the start reconstructs exact historical state, which makes the paper-trading record fully auditable and the runtime testable for determinism.

tour.title: Stage 6 - Execution & The Alpaca Adapter
tour.description: The final stage applies admitted decisions to the portfolio. The pure execution engine turns guard-approved buys into deterministic ExecutionRecords and updates portfolio state, while runtime.py persists that state. Orders leave through the ExecutionPort protocol: the SimulatedBrokerAdapter produces replayable fills for offline paper trading, and the Alpaca adapter submits real market buys to Alpaca's paper API with strict paper-only base-URL guards.
tour.languageLesson: ExecutionPort is a Python Protocol (structural typing): any class with the right method shape satisfies it, no inheritance required. This ports-and-adapters design lets the simulated and Alpaca brokers be swapped without touching the engine, which is why the same pipeline runs both offline and against live paper trading.

tour.title: Risk Guardrails & Supervisor
tour.description: Cross-cutting the pipeline is the risk-control layer. The guardrail engine loads config from the environment and evaluates an ordered chain of trade-validation predicates, returning the first blocking decision or an approval — the safety net the orchestrator consults before any execution. The supervisor decision engine sits above this, scoring candidate strategy upgrades against an evaluation scorecard under treasury and institutional-memory constraints. The dev_graph gates and predicates document the formal contracts these enforce.

tour.title: Operations Control Plane Console
tour.description: The ops console is the human operator's entry point and a tightly coupled cluster in its own right. app.py renders a Textual/Rich multi-tab TUI; core.py is a headless governed read-model that assembles the dashboard purely from src/ functions without reimplementing safety logic; and actions.py and gated.py split operator commands into safe versus confirmation-gated, side-effecting actions such as running the chain against the live Alpaca paper adapter. This layer is how the deterministic engine from Steps 3-10 is actually driven and supervised.
tour.languageLesson: core.py never reimplements trading logic — it only re-reads governed functions from src/. This read-model separation (a CQRS-style split between querying state for display and commanding state changes) keeps the TUI from ever becoming a second, divergent source of safety rules.

tour.title: JARVIS HUD & GraphRAG Backend
tour.description: JARVIS is the project's visual operator surface. The React/Vite MainHud page composes every panel and wires the speech, voice-bridge, Claude-uplink, and graph hooks together, all sharing the central TypeScript type definitions for graph nodes and edges. Behind it, a read-only FastAPI backend bridges Neo4j to expose graph traversal endpoints and a fail-closed GraphRAG /ask route, turning the engineering knowledge graph into an interactive, queryable console.
tour.languageLesson: types.ts is a shared contract imported by components, hooks, and the data router alike — the single highest fan-in TypeScript module. Centralizing type definitions like this means a change to the graph node shape surfaces as compile errors everywhere it is consumed, rather than as silent runtime bugs.

tour.title: Containerization & Deployment
tour.description: The JARVIS backend ships as a container. The Dockerfile builds a single-stage image that installs Python dependencies, copies app.py, and serves the read-only FastAPI graph API with uvicorn on port 8000 over the dev_graph in Neo4j. The compose file orchestrates the full offline-first stack — a Neo4j 5 graph store with APOC, the FastAPI traversal API, and an nginx static frontend — wired together by health-checked dependencies.
tour.languageLesson: docker-compose uses depends_on with health checks so the API only starts once Neo4j reports healthy, and named volumes persist the graph store across restarts. Network isolation between the Neo4j, API, and frontend services keeps the database unreachable from outside the compose network.

tour.title: The Dev Graph Engineering Twin
tour.description: The tour ends where it began — the dev_graph that documents everything you have read. The Layer Model and Context Map you started with are part of an ontology-governed digital twin of ADRs, systems, capabilities, module/file/test nodes, interfaces, and benchmarks that trace every implementation decision back to its rationale. Revisiting it now, with the pipeline understood, shows how the project keeps its code, decisions, and knowledge in lockstep.
